messages:
mira: Heads-up — seeing NVLink link flaps + PCIe AER on gpu-cc-12, us-west2. Multi-GPU jobs down ~30% throughput since 03:12UTC. Posting logs and quick triage notes here.

raj-oncall: :eyes: can you paste dmesg + nvidia-smi? any user impact (errors, OOMs, Xid)?

mira: user impact = degraded perf only, no OOMs. attaching quick snippets.

```
[  845.123456] pci 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[  845.123459] pcieport 0000:64:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorr Error
[  846.000001] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  846.000012] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: nvlink: link0 down
[  846.000130] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: nvlink: link0 up
[  847.000141] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: nvlink: link0 down
```

mira: nvidia-smi topo -m shows missing NVLink between GPU0<->GPU1 intermittently. Perf counters show high PCIe correctable errors on bus 65:00.

infra-bot: Automated check: node gpu-cc-12: memory OK, fans OK, power draw normal. ECC errors++ on GPU0 over last 24h (delta +420).

ben: This reads like AER + NVLink flapping — two routes: software reset/rebind PCI device, or drain and RMA. Given throughput hit, recommend drain + swap if flaps continue after soft-reboot.

chao: Try soft steps first: 1) restart nvidia-persistenced 2) unbind/bind PCI device 3) trigger GPU reset via nvidia-smi --gpu-reset (if supported) 4) check kernel pcie_aspm settings. If flaps persist, escalate HW.

mira: ran restart of persistenced, then:

```
$ sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
$ echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:65:00.0/reset
# got: Permission granted but bus reported AER again
```
Result: flaps resumed within ~2m.

raj-oncall: Can you run a short synthetic multi-GPU workload to reproduce perf regression and capture perf counters? Put on maintenance mode so customers aren't allocated there.

mira: started perf run; 30% drop in throughput, NVLink retries spiking. I cordoned the node already.

ben: Steps to evacuate:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-cc-12
kubectl drain gpu-cc-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Do we have spare capacity in us-west2 to absorb jobs?

infra-bot: us-west2 pool has 4 spare GPUs across spare nodes; autoscaler won't trigger today due to commit limits. Recommend manual shift.

carla-hw: NVLink link flap + repeated AER suggests hardware margin issue or riser/slot contact. If soft recovery fails we should swap the GPU out and run it on a test bench with different host to narrow root cause. Also check PCIe lane widths (lspci -vv) and riser firmware.

mira: lspci -vv snippet:

```
65:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation Device 1eb8 (rev a1)	Subsystem: NVIDIA Corporation Device 1458	LnkSta: Speed 16GT/s, Width x16, TrErr- Train- SlotClk+
```

chao: If LnkSta shows Width x16 and still flapping, less likely a lane count issue. Could be signal integrity — try reseating GPU + power cycle. Schedule a cold power cycle window?

ben: These are prod nodes. If we cold-power-cycle, we must move workloads first. Since node is cordoned/drained, schedule replacement during maintenance window asap.

mira: created ticket HW-3421: "gpu-cc-12 NVLink/AER intermittent — candidate RMA". Assigning to carla-hw.

carla-hw: I'll pick up HW-3421. Plan: 1) replicate on bench 2) try in another host + PCIe slot 3) if failure follows GPU -> RMA 4) if stays host-specific -> check riser/mobo/fabric.

chao: For triage artifacts, please add: dmesg full dump, lspci -vv for all GPUs, nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PCI,POWER,SM, and nvlink status (`nvidia-smi nvlink -s` on supported drivers). Also capture nvml counters.

mira: uploaded logs to /mnt/logs/gpu-cc-12/1750001234/ (dmesg,nvidia-smi-q.txt,lspci-vv.txt,nvlink.log,perf-run.csv).

raj-oncall: Good. For short-term mitigation, set scheduling policy to avoid multi-GPU colocations on that node and mark for no-new-work. ben, can you temporarily reduce multi-GPU placement in the scheduler?

ben: Yep, will add a placement constraint to avoid gpu-cc-12 and set node as unschedulable for multi-gpu jobs.

devops-bot: Action created: #HW-3421 assigned -> carla-hw, priority P2. Maintenance window proposed: 2026-03-19 02:00-03:00 UTC.

mira: Follow-up decision: drain complete, perf tests re-run on new node show baseline restored. We'll keep gpu-cc-12 offline pending bench RMA. Noting: if ECC correctables keep rising after bench swap, open escalation to vendor.

carla-hw: On bench replicate scheduled. I'll post bench results and final disposition in HW-3421. cc: @raj-oncall @ben

mira: thanks team. closing loop here once RMA done. :white_check_mark:
